name: Sikkim
metaTitle: Clinic & Hospital Management Software in Sikkim | Lucoze
metaDescription: Healthcare management software for clinics and hospitals across Sikkim — Gangtok, Namchi, Gyalshing, Mangan, Rangpo. ABDM/ABHA, DPDP 2023, and all patient data hosted in India.
h1Parts: , that runs on an ordinary connection.
lead: Lucoze puts records, appointments, GST billing, lab and pharmacy on one cloud platform — so a patient's history follows them from a Gangtok referral desk to a clinic in Namchi or Mangan. It runs on ordinary broadband or mobile data, and every byte of patient data is hosted in India.
intro: In a small Himalayan state, geography does most of the damage. Towns are spread across ridges, travel between them takes hours, and a patient seen in Gangtok this month may be back near Gyalshing or Rangpo the next — usually carrying a paper file, if anything. A record that lives in the cloud and follows the patient is worth more here than in a flat, dense city. Lucoze is a lightweight tool built for exactly that: one clinic or a small hospital, a front desk that mostly works in English, and a connection that isn't always fast but is usually there.
points: Records that follow the patient across the state
A history started at a Gangtok referral centre is the same record a clinic in Namchi or Mangan opens later. No re-registration, no lost paper file after a long journey down the valley.
Runs on the connection you already have

Lucoze is cloud-based and lightweight — ordinary broadband or mobile data is enough. It is not an offline app, so you do need a working connection, but it is built to stay usable when the line is slow, not just when it's fast.
English at the desk, and search that isn't fussy

Clinics here mostly run in English, and Lucoze works fully in English today. Patient search matches Devanagari and Latin spellings, so a Nepali name typed either way still finds the record. A Nepali or Sikkimese interface isn't available — the UI rolls out in Hindi first (Q3 2026), then Bengali and Odia — so we're upfront: printable cheat-sheets cover your staff in the meantime.
ABDM, GST and scheme-ready, data kept in India

Issue an ABHA at the first visit, generate GST-compliant invoices, and keep clean records for Ayushman Bharat (PMJAY) and state schemes. Everything is built for DPDP 2023, hosted in Indian data centres, with full CSV/PDF export and no lock-in.
localContext: We're set up for clinics and small hospitals across Sikkim — Gangtok's referral desks and OPDs around MG Marg, Tadong and Ranipool, plus standalone practices in Namchi, Gyalshing, Mangan, Rangpo and Singtam. Sikkim's medicine is spread thin across the hills: a few busy centres in and around the capital, and smaller clinics a long drive apart. English is the common language at the desk, with Nepali, Sikkimese/Bhutia and Lepcha spoken among patients — so Devanagari-and-Latin patient search plus printable cheat-sheets matter more here than a translated menu. Because the towns are far-flung and mountainous, we run remote-first: video onboarding, migration help and support over WhatsApp and chat, rather than pretending we'll drive to every valley.

faqs.a: Yes — Lucoze runs fully in English today, which is how most Sikkim clinic desks already work. The interface rolls out in Hindi first (Q3 2026), then Bengali and Odia; a Nepali or Sikkimese interface isn't planned yet. Patient search handles Devanagari and Latin spellings, and we include printable front-desk cheat-sheets.

faqs.q: Where is our patient data stored?
faqs.a: In Indian data centres, with backups kept in India — nothing crosses the border. Lucoze is built for DPDP 2023, and you can export all your records as CSV or PDF on request, with no lock-in.

faqs.q: Do you support clinics in Sikkim, given you're based in West Bengal?
faqs.a: Yes. Our team is in Konnagar, Hooghly, so for a far-flung, mountainous state we work remote-first: video onboarding, data-migration help, WhatsApp and chat support, plus printable cheat-sheets. On-site visits are reserved for larger hospital deployments. There's a 14-day trial, and most clinics go live within 14 days.
